  \[
  f = [11250,\, 13480,\, 14870,\, 10290,\, 16740,\, 13960,\, 12680,\, 17890,\, 10950,\, 15320,\, 11830,\, 14110,\, 15970,\, 13140,\, 10580]
  \]
  where \( f_i \) is the fixed cost for plant \( i \).

  \[
  K = [101,\, 124,\, 139,\, 86,\, 157,\, 133,\, 118,\, 162,\, 92,\, 144,\, 107,\, 129,\, 151,\, 113,\, 85]

  where \( K_i \) is the capacity of plant \( i \).

  where \( d_j \) is the demand of customer \( j \).

Decision variables:
- \( y_i \in \{0,1\} \): 1 if plant \( i \) is built (opened), 0 otherwise.
- \( x_{ij} \geq 0 \): amount shipped from plant \( i \) to customer \( j \).

Mathematical Model:

\[
\begin{align*}
\text{Minimize} \quad & \sum_{i=1}^{15} f_i y_i + \sum_{i=1}^{15} \sum_{j=1}^{15} c_{ij} x_{ij} \\

& x_{ij} \geq 0 \quad \forall i, j \\
& y_i \in \{0,1\} \quad \forall i
\end{align*}
\]

- \( f_i \), \( K_i \), \( d_j \), and \( c_{ij} \) are as listed above.

Once a plant is opened, it may supply products to any customers, subject to its own capacity.

    There are 15 customers C1–C15 with fixed demands. If a plant is built, it incurs the fixed cost and can distribute to any number of customers. Shipping from plant i to customer j incurs a per-unit transport cost. The objective is to determine which plants should be built and how much to ship from each built plant to each customer in order to minimize the total cost, consisting of both fixed opening costs and variable transportation costs, while satisfying all customer demands and not exceeding the capacities of the opened plants.

    The input data are given in two CSV files. cost.csv includes fixed_cost: opening cost of the plant (currency units; paid once if the plant is opened, regardless of the number of customers served). And capacity: plant capacity (maximum units the plant can supply). And also C1 … C15: per-unit transport cost from this plant to each customer. demand.csv includes demand of the customer (units) (C1-C15)


Build a self-contained program using the concrete coefficients and identifiers in
the Mathematical Optimization Model / Retrieved Information and Original Query.
Define all required data in the code. Do not use CSVQA_DATA, external variables,
or external files.


Preserve facility-opening and assignment indices and their linking constraints.

Leave the solved Gurobi model in m or model. If using a function, return the model
and assign it to m. Set MIPGap=1e-4 before optimize().

Give each decision-variable container a distinct name ending in _vars; never reuse it as a loop variable, scalar key, parameter or row object. In a generator expression, index the decision container with the locally bound key, not with a shadowed container. quicksum takes an iterable; a scalar constant is used directly.
